clue.text: The cleaner is attracting mother, so must have this

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the quality someone attracting others must have

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, short for charwoman

explanation.surface: A cleaner draws admirers, as well as her mother, so she must have some special quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: anyone attracting people must have CHARISMA. A char is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, the very quality that lets someone attract others.

clue.text: Shrewd plea to keep a "Financial Times"

indicators.note: one word holds the others inside itself, as a box keeps its contents

parts.note: a cry is an appeal or plea
the usual abbreviation for the newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone asks shrewdly to hang on to a copy of the business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty and shrewd are both synonyms for cunning or astute.

clue.text: Stay in Anglican Choristers

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of following words, spanning a word break

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A choirboy is staying on in a church choir.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is a support or mainstay, something that keeps a thing steady, like a stay.

clue.text: Apply for tinned spread

indicators.note: the letters are spread around and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to request some canned spread, like paste or pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a noun to be canned, but it is the signal to rearrange 'tinned'.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent for goods is to place an official order or requisition for them.

clue.text: £500 leads to legal action for formal diner

definitions.note: really clothing for a formal dinner, playing on 'diner' as dinner wear

parts.note: British slang for five hundred pounds

explanation.surface: Losing a large sum ends in a lawsuit against a smartly dressed restaurant guest.
explanation.walkthrough: A monkey is British slang for £500. The definition is loose: the answer is what a formal diner wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey suit is slang for a dinner jacket or tuxedo, worn at formal dinners.

clue.text: Sound of brass returns with chance to get sound of cow

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck

explanation.surface: A brass band's noise comes back, and it might sound like a lowing cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' applies to the whole joined string, not just the first word; hap is an archaic word that survives in 'happen' and 'mishap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah is the imitative word for the deep rhythmic thump of a tuba or brass band.

clue.text: Member of small government breaks chair with log

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and its parts end up in a different order

explanation.surface: A minor politician smashes a chair with a log.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of the few people who rule in an oligarchy, government by a small group.

clue.text: "Ace pilot crashed" — written in verse

indicators.note: a crashed plane is wrecked, its parts scattered into a jumble

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a flying ace's crash, delivered in rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetical means relating to or composed as poetry, that is, in metrical lines.

clue.text: Understanding discomfort and worry

parts.note: as in having a head for figures, an aptitude or understanding

explanation.surface: A list of the symptoms of stress: grasping the problem, feeling unwell, fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is figuratively a troublesome problem or source of anxiety.

clue.text: A misfortune, identity in stress

indicators.note: one item placed inside another, so the second word wraps around the first

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
short for identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: Someone under strain suffers a mishap with their sense of self.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky, unplanned event, a mishap or misfortune.

clue.text: Came in, interpreting films

indicators.note: interpreting means rendering something in a new form, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: A critic arrived to give their reading of some movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema as a collective noun means the art or industry of films.

clue.text: Punished, but sadly not cured

indicators.note: something going sadly goes wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A patient was penalised, yet unfortunately remained ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat or thrash soundly, a harsh punishment.

clue.text: Sesame-seed paste mixed in a hat

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A cook stirs up a dip in an odd container: a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahina, or tahini, is the Middle Eastern paste ground from sesame seeds.

clue.text: E.g. flat and thirsty, having succeeded

parts.note: a flat is an example of a home
dry can mean wanting a drink

explanation.surface: Someone describes their state: in a flat, parched, but victorious.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat is the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Home and dry is a British idiom meaning safely through, having achieved one's aim.

clue.text: He keeps others waiting in a snail-like charabanc

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sluggish person others must wait for
second meaning, literal: a coach that moves at a snail's pace

explanation.surface: A dawdler holds everyone up on a slow-moving bus trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person who is slow to act or understand, holding others up.

clue.text: Poverty made Hardy almost get on steamer?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the name stops one letter short

parts.note: the novelist's name without its final letter
a steamer is a kind of ship

explanation.surface: Poverty drove the novelist Thomas Hardy nearly to board a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship means suffering caused by want, such as poverty or deprivation.

clue.text: First girl on railway, unique in all the world

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis
one, as in 'one of a kind'

explanation.surface: A train's first female passenger is uniquely remarkable across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: All the world is an idiom for every person, everybody.

clue.text: Openings for girl participating in broadcasts

indicators.note: a participant takes part inside an activity, so one word goes within the other

explanation.surface: Chances for a young woman to take part in radio or TV programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crannies are small narrow gaps or chinks, openings in a wall or rock.

clue.text: I've traders coming around?

indicators.note: coming around suggests turning about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that the merchants are calling round.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone who advertises might hope to say that traders are coming round to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser publicises goods, drawing in customers and dealers who come round in response.

clue.text: Need to be right when cutting up curtains?

indicators.note: cutting into something goes inside it; in a down clue the letter enters from below

parts.note: 'curtains' is slang for the end, death

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to have the correct side when trimming drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' looks like soft furnishings, but it is slang for the end of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, a state of want or need.

clue.text: Bobs up and down with a wife which is a puzzle

parts.note: jigs means jumps or bobs about

explanation.surface: Someone bounces about with their spouse, which is baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture cut into pieces to be fitted back together, a type of puzzle.

clue.text: Act like Professor Higgins, making another day fly

indicators.note: making another version of something produces a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Henry Higgins of Pygmalion makes the time pass quickly for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Higgins, in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, turns flower girl Eliza Doolittle into a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladyfy is to make a lady of someone, exactly what Higgins does to Eliza.

clue.text: Plucky daughter takes a phone call

parts.note: to give someone a ring is to phone them

explanation.surface: A brave girl answers the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and plucky are both synonyms for bold or courageous.

clue.text: Decoration used on cake, lovely one

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Praise for a beautiful cake topping.
explanation.walkthrough: Angelica stems are candied and cut into green strips to decorate cakes in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied angelica stalks are a traditional green garnish used to decorate cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Nearly hoot, then die, in a sweatshirt

indicators.note: nearly means falling just short, so the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: the word lacking its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone almost laughs themselves to death while wearing a sweatshirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodie is a hooded sweatshirt, so the general garment stands for it.

clue.text: It is probable that Ida will have unsettled years

indicators.note: unsettled things are disturbed from their place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prediction that a woman called Ida faces a turbulent time ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I dare say' is a phrase admitting that something is likely or very possibly so.

clue.text: Pray as peel is chopped up

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into bits that can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook asks for a prayer while the orange skin is sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pray' is the old polite word used in requests, as in 'pray be seated', not an act of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pray, as a courteous request, carries the same meaning as the request word for asking kindly.

clue.text: Incidentally, it's next to the track

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a passing remark
second meaning, literal: beside the road or path

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: something positioned beside a path.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom introducing a side remark, while literally meaning alongside a road.
